{{Short description|Theorem in complex analysis}}
In [[mathematics]], specifically [[complex analysis]], '''Riemann's existence theorem''' states that the category of [[compact space|compact]] [[Riemann surface]]s is equivalent to the category of complex [[complete algebraic curve]]s.

Sometimes, the theorem also refers to a generalization (a theorem of Grauert–Remmert),<ref> SGA 1, Expose XII, Théorème 5.1.</ref> which says that the category of finite topological coverings of a complex [[algebraic variety]] is equivalent to the category  of finite étale coverings of the variety.

==Original statement==
Let <math>X</math> be a compact Riemann surface, <math>p_1, \cdots, p_s</math> distinct points in <math>X</math> and <math>a_1, \cdots, a_s</math> complex numbers. Then there is a [[meromorphic function]] <math>f</math> on <math>X</math> such that <math>f(p_i) = a_i</math> for all <math>1\leq i\leq s</math>.<ref>Theorem 1.2. in Ishan Levy, Galois theory and Riemann surfaces. [https://ishanina.github.io/PROMYS/Galois%20Theory%20and%20Riemann%20Surfaces/Galois_Theory_and_Riemann_Surfaces.html]</ref>

== Proof ==
{{expand section|date=June 2025}}

For now, see SGA 1, Expose XII, Théorème 5.1., or SGA 4, Expose XI. 4.3.

== Consequences ==
By definition, if <math>X</math> is a complex algebraic variety, the [[étale fundamental group]] of <math>X</math> at a geometric point <math>x</math> is the [[projective limit]]
:<math>\pi_1^{\textrm{et}}(X, x) = \varprojlim \operatorname{Aut}_X(Y)</math>
over all finite Galois coverings <math>Y</math> of <math>X</math>. By the existence theorem, we have
:<math>\operatorname{Aut}_X(Y) = \operatorname{Aut}_{X^{an}}(Y^{an})</math>.
Hence, <math>\pi_1^{\textrm{et}}(X, x)</math> is exactly the profinite completion of the usual topological [[fundamental group]] <math>\pi_1(X^{\textrm{an}}, x)</math> of <math>X</math> at <math>x</math>.<ref>{{harvnb|Milne|loc=A subsection called "Varieties over <math>\mathbb C</math>" after Remark 3.3.}}</ref>
